CONTEXT. The previous page, this page and the next page form one table. It covers the primes p ≡ 1 (mod 8) in order: 401?, 409, 433, 449, 457, 521, 569, 577, 593, 601, 617, 641, 673, 761. For each p Gauss handles the binary quadratic forms (a,b,c) = ax²+2bxy+cy² of determinant b²−ac = −p.

THE INDEX ROWS. The two-row bracket {0 1 2 … ; 2m 2m−1 …} labels the classes as powers g^k of a generator g. So he takes the class group of order h = h(−4p) to be cyclic. Class k is paired with its inverse h−k, because opposite forms represent the same numbers. The self-paired entries Cl.0 and Cl.h/2 are the two ambiguous classes.

The orders read off the brackets are:
- 409 → 16; 433 → 12; 449 → 20; 457 → 8;
- 521 → 32; 569 → 32; 577 → 8; 593 → 24;
- 601 → 20; 617 → 12; 641 → 28; 673 → 12; 761 → 40.

THREE-SQUARE DECOMPOSITIONS. Against each even class (the principal genus, i.e. the squares) Gauss writes a decomposition p = x²+y²+z². This is the correspondence of Disq. Arith. arts. 278–292: decompositions up to order and sign correspond one-to-one to pairs {K, K⁻¹} of classes in the principal genus. The decomposition with a 0 (p as a sum of two squares) goes to Cl.0. The decomposition with two equal squares goes to the ambiguous class Cl.h/2. Since r₃(p) = 12·h(−4p), the number of decompositions must be h/4 + 1.

NUMBERS AFTER 'c:'. These are small primes q represented by the class, i.e. q = a of a reduced form in that class. The primes in odd classes are all ≡ 3 (mod 4). Those in even classes are ≡ 1 (mod 4), plus 2 in the ambiguous class Cl.h/2. This fits the genus character n ↦ (−1)^((n−1)/2) for determinant −p with p ≡ 1 (mod 8).

PURPOSE. This is an empirical table of the class groups of the forms of determinant −p for primes p ≡ 1 (mod 8). For each p it gives:
- the class number;
- cyclicity, with an explicit generator given by a small prime;
- the representatives of the classes by small primes;
- the bijection between three-square decompositions of p and the classes of the principal genus.
errors: No arithmetic errors found. Every three-square sum on the page equals its p (521, 569, 593).
For each of 521, 569 and 593 the list of decompositions is complete, and the counts are h/4+1 as required.
Every listed prime q satisfies (−p/q) = 1 and has the genus character expected for the parity of its class.
Some table entries are incomplete, not wrong: 577 and 601 are unfinished skeletons, and some classes of 569 and 593 have no prime listed.

results.what: Table of class numbers h(−4p) of forms of determinant −p for primes p ≡ 1 mod 8, with the class group taken to be cyclic and indexed by powers of a generator represented by a small prime (e.g. 3).
results.modern_name: Class group Cl(−4p) of binary quadratic forms; class number tables
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones 1801; Nachlass tables published in Werke II)

results.what: Bijection between decompositions p = x²+y²+z² (up to order and sign) and pairs of inverse classes in the principal genus; the two-square decomposition goes to the principal class and the decomposition with a repeated square to the ambiguous class; count check r₃(p) = 12h.
results.modern_name: Gauss's three-squares theorem and class number formula r₃(n) = 12h(−4n) (n ≡ 1,2 mod 4)

results.what: Small primes represented by each class, used to identify the classes; their residues mod 4 match the genus characters.
results.modern_name: Prime representatives of ideal classes / genus theory

deep.surprise_reason: This is numerical tabulation squarely within Gauss's published theory of ternary and binary forms (Disquisitiones arts. 278–292) and his known class-number tables. The explicit matching of each three-square decomposition to a power of a generator is a nice unpublished computational detail, but it contains no new theorem.
